content.value_statement: Stakeholder disagreements often hide valid concerns on both sides. This skill helps Claude, Codex, or Claude Code build a structured synthesis with explicit trade-offs.
actual_capabilities: Frames a thesis with position, stakeholder, evidence, implications, risks, and benefits.
Builds an antithesis that challenges assumptions and presents counter evidence.
Creates synthesis through integration, sequencing, segmentation, reframing, or transcendence.
Documents trade-offs, mitigations, and the stakeholder who accepts each cost.
Defines implementation actions, metrics, and review dates for the integrated position.
limitations: Depends on user-provided evidence and does not verify factual claims independently.
Requires genuinely opposed positions, not a simple cause-effect question.
Cannot guarantee stakeholder agreement; it provides a structured protocol.
May produce abstract synthesis when constraints, incentives, or decision criteria are missing.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Product Investment
use_cases.description: Compare competing product bets, surface stakeholder incentives, and choose an integrated roadmap direction.

use_cases.title: Align Executive Decisions
use_cases.description: Turn opposing leadership positions into a shared decision with clear trade-offs and review metrics.

use_cases.title: Resolve Program Planning Disputes
use_cases.description: Balance delivery pressure, technical debt, and team capacity without ignoring any core concern.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Two-Sided Decision
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner analysis for a clear disagreement.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use dialectical reasoning for this decision: [decision]. Thesis: [first position]. Antithesis: [opposing position]. Identify evidence, concerns, synthesis, and trade-offs.

prompt_templates.title: Stakeholder Position Map
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate analysis with known teams or roles.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this stakeholder conflict with a thesis, antithesis, and synthesis. For each side, include role, incentives, evidence, risks, benefits, and underlying concern.

prompt_templates.title: Strategic Trade-Off Resolution
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced decision support for resource allocation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a dialectical synthesis for this strategic trade-off: [context]. Test integration, sequencing, segmentation, reframing, and transcendence before recommending one path.

prompt_templates.title: Implementation-Ready Synthesis
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced output for decisions that need execution.
prompt_templates.prompt: Produce a full dialectical output with thesis, antithesis, synthesis, acknowledged trade-offs, stakeholder agreement conditions, implementation actions, metrics, and review date.

output_examples.input: Engineering wants a platform rebuild. Sales wants Q2 customer features.
output_examples.output: The synthesis recommends incremental rebuild work tied to high-priority feature delivery. Engineering accepts a longer rebuild timeline, while Sales accepts a smaller Q2 feature set.

output_examples.input: A team debates enterprise focus versus SMB growth.
output_examples.output: The skill reframes the issue as revenue efficiency plus learning velocity. It proposes using SMB feedback to validate features before enterprise rollout.

output_examples.input: Two departments disagree about whether to centralize a process.
output_examples.output: The output identifies each department concern, validates both positions, and proposes segmentation with shared metrics and a review date.

best_practices: Provide real evidence for both positions before asking for synthesis.
Name stakeholders and incentives so the analysis does not become abstract.
Require explicit trade-offs, owners, metrics, and review dates.
anti_patterns: Using the skill to force a predetermined answer.
Treating synthesis as a simple compromise between two positions.
Skipping implementation details after agreeing on a high-level position.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps an AI assistant synthesize opposing positions into an integrated decision with trade-offs and next steps.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when two or more valid perspectives conflict and a decision needs shared reasoning.

faq.question: Does it verify the evidence?
faq.answer: No. It organizes and evaluates evidence that you provide, but it does not independently validate facts.

faq.question: Is this only for business strategy?
faq.answer: No. It can support product, planning, policy, design, and organizational decisions.

faq.question: How is synthesis different from compromise?
faq.answer: Synthesis integrates the core concerns behind each position. Compromise often splits the difference without resolving the tension.

faq.question: What input works best?
faq.answer: Provide each position, the stakeholder behind it, supporting evidence, constraints, risks, and desired outcome.
